olivia.keller: Heads-up — Procurement asked me to run a quick eval of SpendWise for invoice reconciliation and supplier analytics. Their pricing is confusing, can someone help parse whether this is seat-based or usage-based?
ashwin.patel: I glanced at their one-pager. They have a base platform fee + per-invoice processing, and an optional seat charge for analytics users. Can you paste the quote?
mike.thompson: Also want to know if they charge for API calls separately — we batch ingestion, so per-API pricing kills the model.
olivia.keller: Copy of the quote from their sales rep below (redacted):
```
- Annual platform fee: $20,000
- Processing: $0.12 per invoice for first 100k, $0.08 thereafter
- Analytics seats: $150/user/month (minimum 3 seats)
- API calls: 5¢ per 1,000 calls beyond 2M free calls/month
- SOC2 + SSO included
- 60-day termination notice, 30-day data export window
```
jessica.chen: Hmm. For us the volume estimate is ~250k invoices/year. Math: 250k * $0.12 = $30k processing + $20k platform = $50k base, seats add if we want non-technical users. That feels pricey vs. other vendors but depends on quality of ML matching.
spendwise_repmike: Hi everyone — Mike from SpendWise. Happy to run a tailored model for Redwood. Two notes: (1) We can move to a blended processing rate if you commit to 12 months. (2) We can waive the seats minimum for enterprise contracts. Would you like a model with a committed invoice tier? :slightly_smiling_face:
ashwin.patel: Yes to a committed tier. Can you show an example with a 12-month 250k commit? Also need clarity on overage caps.
spendwise_repmike: Example committed pricing (12mo, 250k/year):
```
- Platform fee: $15,000/year (discounted)
- Committed processing: $0.10/invoice for first 250k = $25,000
- Overage: $0.06/invoice above committed tier (billing monthly)
- Analytics seats: $0 (included for up to 5 viewers)
- API: 2M free calls/month included, overage at $0.03/1k
- Contract: 12mo term, 45-day termination notice for convenience
```
mike.thompson: That actually lands around $40k/yr, which is reasonable. Need procurement to confirm PO/contract flow, and security sign-off on data retention.
jessica.chen: Can we get a trial to validate matching accuracy? If ML match rate is poor we should ask for SLA credits.
spendwise_repmike: We can offer a 30-day pilot with up to 10k invoices ingested. If match rate < 95% on agreed test set, we provide a 20% credit for the first paid month.
olivia.keller: Sounds good. Procurement asks: do they accept our standard PO language (net 45) and can they sign a mutual NDA + amendment for vendor data access?
spendwise_repmike: We accept net 45 and can sign the NDA. We typically ask for a standard vendor addendum for data export guarantees; happy to review your language.
procurement-bot: Reminder: To push this through, procurement needs: (1) final SOW with committed volumes, (2) redlined contract or approval to use vendor standard with addendum, (3) SOC2 report and security questionnaire completed. Upload to /procurement/vendor-docs.
ashwin.patel: I'll draft the SOW with the 250k commit and include expected monthly ingestion cadence. Olivia — can you coordinate the pilot data sample and the security questionnaire?
olivia.keller: On it. I'll upload a sanitized sample and loop in security for the questionnaire. Thanks everyone — will circle back once pilot starts. :thumbsup:
